title: Claude Cowork & Autonomous Desktop Agents
content:
## Overview

Claude Cowork is Anthropic's autonomous desktop agent, released as a research preview in January 2026 and moved to general availability on April 9, 2026 (alongside the public beta of Claude Managed Agents). Where Claude Code targets developers working in a terminal or IDE, Cowork targets non-technical users working with everyday files — spreadsheets, slide decks, PDFs, folders of documents.

---

## How It Works

Users grant Cowork permission-based access to specific folders on their computer through the Claude macOS desktop app. Instead of returning suggestions or a chat answer, Cowork executes the work directly:

1. Reads the relevant files in the granted folder(s)
2. Builds a plan and breaks the task into parallel subtasks
3. Produces finished output files (an Excel workbook with working formulas, a PowerPoint deck, a Word document, extracted data from scanned PDFs, a synthesis across dozens of source files)

**Typical tasks:** file organization, spreadsheet and slide generation, data extraction from images/PDFs, and multi-document research synthesis.

---

## Architecture: Isolated VM

Cowork runs inside an isolated virtual machine using Apple's Virtualization Framework, booting a custom Linux filesystem rather than acting directly on the host macOS environment. This sandboxing is the safety boundary that lets Cowork take autonomous, multi-step action on real user files without each step requiring a fresh permission prompt — access is scoped to the folders the user explicitly grants up front.

**Model defaults differ by product:** Cowork defaults to Opus-tier models for better autonomous task handling, while Claude Code defaults to a faster Sonnet-tier model tuned for interactive coding sessions. Both can be reconfigured.

---

## Computer Use and Scheduled Tasks

Cowork's computer-use mode (research preview, Pro/Max plans) lets Claude drive a real browser, open applications, and operate dev tools with no additional setup — extending beyond file-only workflows into full desktop automation.

**Scheduled tasks** let a Cowork workflow run automatically on a recurring basis without the user re-invoking it each time — the same underlying capability that powers scheduled Claude Code prompts (see the Claude Code Overview page), but aimed at office-document workflows instead of code repositories.

---

## Enterprise Features (GA, April 2026)

The general-availability release paired Cowork with six enterprise features aimed at IT/security teams adopting it at scale:

- **RBAC** (role-based access control) over who can run Cowork and against which folders
- **OpenTelemetry** integration for observability into agent runs
- **Zoom MCP** connector, demonstrating Cowork consuming an MCP server the same way Claude Code does

---

## Claude Code Security: The Developer-Side Counterpart

Running alongside Cowork's rollout, Anthropic shipped **Claude Code Security** — a multi-agent vulnerability scanner that lives inside Claude Code rather than the desktop app:

- Limited research preview: February 20, 2026 (Enterprise/Team)
- Public beta: April 30, 2026, open to all Claude Enterprise customers
- Originally powered by **Opus 4.7**; upgraded in mid-2026 to run on **Claude Mythos 5**, the specialized vulnerability-research model also used internally by Anthropic's security consortium

Rather than matching code against a database of known CVE patterns, it reasons about how components interact and how data flows through the application, then re-verifies each candidate finding in a multi-stage pass to suppress false positives before assigning a severity rating.

---

## Why This Matters

Cowork and Claude Code Security represent Anthropic's push to extend agentic capability past the terminal: one product automates general office work end-to-end inside a sandboxed VM, the other embeds security review directly into the developer's existing Claude Code workflow. Both lean on the same underlying model family (Opus/Sonnet-tier reasoning, MCP for external tool access) that powers Claude Code itself.
